notes: Browser = ShopCouponsPage + couponService + Axios. Account holder may have any role; the expanded successful request is SHOP_MANAGER. A denied request stops immediately: later messages belong only to the permitted path. Errors return through NestJS exception handling; no controller call occurs after guard rejection.

NestJS pipeline is a framework participant. JWT self-messages summarize Passport + JwtStrategy + Prisma delegation. Invalid/missing/expired JWT or absent/inactive/deleted User: 401 before RolesGuard. Passport sets request.user from the reloaded User; its database role governs access.

@Roles stores metadata under ROLES_KEY = roles. Reflector reads handler first, then controller. Missing metadata or an empty role array returns true immediately; RolesGuard alone does not authenticate. Non-empty roles plus missing request.user or role mismatch: 403. No role hierarchy or automatic Admin bypass exists.

Actual coupon RBAC examples: Admin createPlatformCoupon = SYSTEM_ADMIN or SYSTEM_MANAGER; Shop createStoreCoupon / approveCoupon = SHOP_MANAGER; KOL proposeCoupon = COLLABORATOR. Store controller metadata also allows Admin/Manager for inherited methods, but approveCoupon overrides that list to SHOP_MANAGER only.

Controller delegates to CouponsService (see FR12): recheck SHOP_MANAGER; require Store.ownerId = userId; apply approval policy and writes. Another Shop owner gets 403; missing Store gets 404. Service internals are omitted. RolesGuard itself performs no DB query, ownership check or KYC check.

Selected protected route only: guards are bound explicitly by @UseGuards, not a universal application-wide policy. FR9 uses its own StoreOwnerGuard. Frontend RoleGuard controls workspace navigation; backend guards enforce API access independently. Library base classes and DTO/pipes/interceptor internals are omitted.
